# Introduction

One compound in an LC-MS experiment gives many features: its protonated or
deprotonated molecule, other adducts such as `[M+Na]+`, in-source fragments
such as `[M+H-H2O]+`, and the isotopes of all of these. Together they form
the compound's *ion family*. Recognising ion families reduces redundancy and
helps to work out the neutral mass of unknown compounds.

`groupFeatures()` from the *MsFeatures* and *xcms* packages groups features
that probably come from the same compound (similar retention time, correlated
abundances across samples, similar peak shapes). It deliberately stops there.
*IonFamilies* takes the groups and annotates, within each group,

1. **isotope patterns**, with `MetaboCoreUtils::isotopologues()`, which checks
   mass differences and intensity ratios, and
2. **adducts and fragments**, by neutral-mass voting with a rule list: a
   neutral mass is suggested when two or more features of a group can be
   explained as different ions of it.

All supported neutral-mass hypotheses are kept and ranked. The annotations
are meant as **hints** for what to check, so the default rule list is long
and recall is preferred over precision. Results are written to the
`featureDefinitions()` of the `XcmsExperiment` in the format CAMERA used
(`pcgroup`, `isotopes`, `adduct`), so existing downstream code keeps working.
The vignette *How neutral-mass voting works* explains the method step by
step.

## Related packages

* *CAMERA* does grouping, isotope and adduct annotation, but works on the
  legacy `xcmsSet` class. *IonFamilies* re-implements its neutral-mass voting
  for `groupFeatures()` groups and keeps all hypotheses, ranked, instead of
  one per feature.
* *InterpretMSSpectrum* (`findMAIN()`) ranks main-adduct hypotheses for a
  single spectrum. *RAMClustR* uses it after its own clustering.
* *cliqueMS* annotates one sample at a time with its own grouping.
* *MetaboAnnotation* matches features against compound databases. It
  complements the database-free annotation here.

# Installation

```{r install}
#| eval: false
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stanstrup/IonFamilies")
```

# Grouping features

We use the small example data set that comes with *xcms*: an
`XcmsExperiment` with peak detection, alignment and correspondence already
done. First the features are grouped by retention time, then the groups are
split by the correlation of the features' abundances across samples.

```{r load}
#| message: false
library(xcms)
library(MsFeatures)
library(IonFamilies)

x <- loadXcmsData("xmse")
x <- groupFeatures(x, SimilarRtimeParam(diffRt = 10))
x <- groupFeatures(x, AbundanceSimilarityParam(threshold = 0.7,
                                               transform = log2))
table(lengths(split(featureGroups(x), featureGroups(x))))
```

With raw data available, `EicSimilarityParam()` would add a third step that
compares peak shapes.

# Isotopes

`annotateIsotopes()` searches isotope patterns within each group. The
representative intensity of a feature is its median over the samples given by
`subset` (all samples by default).

```{r isotopes}
x <- annotateIsotopes(x, IsotopologueParam(ppm = 10, tolerance = 0.005))
fd <- featureDefinitions(x)
head(fd[fd$isotopes != "", c("mzmed", "rtmed", "feature_group", "isotopes")])
```

`isIsotopologue()` identifies the heavy isotopologues, for example to remove
them before statistics:

```{r is-isotopologue}
table(isIsotopologue(fd$isotopes))
```

# Adducts and fragments

`annotateAdducts()` uses the rules in `defaultAdductRules()`, which come from
the *commonMZ* package and are expanded to one to four molecules per ion.

```{r rules}
rules <- defaultAdductRules("positive")
nrow(rules)
head(rules)
```

`nBest` sets how many hypotheses per feature are written to the `adduct`
column. All of them are stored in any case.

```{r adducts}
x <- annotateAdducts(x, AdductVoteParam(polarity = "positive", nBest = 2))
fd <- featureDefinitions(x)
head(fd[fd$adduct != "", c("mzmed", "pcgroup", "isotopes", "adduct")])
```

The full table of hypotheses, one row per hypothesis and feature, is
returned by `adductHints()`. `rank` is the rank of the hypothesis for that
feature and `n_ions` the number of features that support the neutral mass.

```{r hints}
hints <- adductHints(x)
head(hints)
```

The text column can be rewritten with another `nBest` without recomputing:

```{r format}
x <- formatAdducts(x, nBest = 1)
head(featureDefinitions(x)$adduct[featureDefinitions(x)$adduct != ""])
```

`bestHypotheses()` reduces the hints to at most one neutral mass per feature,
as CAMERA's final result did:

```{r best}
head(bestHypotheses(hints))
```

The parameters used are stored in the object:

```{r params}
S4Vectors::metadata(x)$IonFamilies
```

# Working with plain vectors

All functions also work without *xcms*. Here are the ions of 2-furoylglycine
(M = 169.0375), a marker of coffee intake, from one feature group:

```{r vectors}
mz <- c(95.0124, 124.0392, 152.0342, 170.0445, 171.0496, 192.0275,
        377.0300, 393.0019)
int <- c(71.6, 81.4, 49.8, 100, 4.33, 11.3, 1.76, 1.82)
grp <- rep("FG.1", length(mz))

iso <- annotateIsotopes(mz, IsotopologueParam(), intensity = int,
                        groups = grp)
hints <- annotateAdducts(mz, AdductVoteParam(), intensity = int,
                         groups = grp, exclude = isIsotopologue(iso))
data.frame(mz, isotopes = iso,
           adduct = formatAdducts(hints, nBest = 2, nFeatures = length(mz)))
```
